t: This is St Botolph without Aldersgate, a Church of England church in the City of London. It was built just outside Aldersgate, one of the gates in London's wall, which explains the name. Several notable people are buried here. John Bradmore was a medieval surgeon and court physician under Henry IV, best known for removing an arrow from the skull of the king's son, the future Henry V, after the Battle of Shrewsbury. Sir John Micklethwaite, a physician to Charles II, lies here too, as does John Tamworth, a courtier, Member of Parliament and ambassador to Scotland.
